## free-tier-llm-landscape
- What matters: free tiers at Groq, Together, OpenRouter, Google Gemini and Hugging Face have historically shifted limits, model availability and terms with little notice; I don’t know current specifics.
- Why it matters: an agent that runs only on free tiers can fail silently when a model is deprecated, rate limits tighten, or a “free” route gains quotas or attribution requirements.
- Verify: check each provider’s current docs and terms for rate limits, model deprecations, commercial-use clauses and whether OpenRouter’s free models still route to the expected providers.

## agent-safety-practice
- What matters: good practice is tiered approval (auto for read-only, human approval for writes, network and destructive actions), strong sandboxing, and treating all fetched content as untrusted.
- Why it matters: autonomous coding agents can be steered by prompt injection in issues, repos or tool output; least privilege and auditability limit blast radius and make incidents reconstructable.
- Verify: confirm sandbox egress allowlists, that creden
